lines.text: Many learners say: My son is very educated.
Better: My son is very polite.
The first! She is polite to me.

native.tip: Para dizer que alguém tem boas maneiras, use “polite”, não “educated”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “My son is very educated.” O certo é “My son is very polite.” Em português “educado” é ser gentil, mas em inglês “educated” fala de estudo. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “She is polite to me.” Agora diga em voz alta uma frase sua com esse ponto e treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: To say someone has good manners, use “polite”, not “educated”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “My son is very educated.” The right way is “My son is very polite.” In Portuguese “educado” means kind, but English “educated” is about schooling. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
